The E-Governance Days

The four editions brought together public authorities, diplomatic missions, international organisations, technology companies, researchers and educators to examine digital governance.

The story Four editions Recommendations 2011 participants 2008 participants Sponsors & partners Archive photographs Personal archive Sources
4editions2008–2011annual series300 → 1,000+From about 300 participants in 2008 to 1,000+ in 2011, according to the departmental report

A documented first

“For the first time in Ukraine”

“For the first time in Ukraine, an E-Governance Day is being held, organised by the National Academy of Public Administration under the President of Ukraine.”

First in the World. According to open sources, no earlier national E-Governance Day has been recorded anywhere. Its status as Ukraine’s first is explicitly attested in UNDP’s greeting published in the official 2008 proceedings.

Open the 2008 proceedings →

The people behind the series

Founders & Organizers

Public sources document the organisers’ formal roles. The account of the forum’s origins is attributed to those involved in the project.

Documented roles

Prof. Svitlana Chukut

Headed the Information Policy Department at the National Academy of Public Administration under the President of Ukraine, which organised the forum. Edited the 128-page 2008 proceedings and co-edited the 2010 proceedings. As an e-governance working group member, she participated in the 17 May 2011 round table. The draft programme also lists her for the 16 May second plenary session, with a talk on master’s-level training in e-governance.

Olha Zahvoiska, PhD

PhD in Public Administration, co-editor of the 2008 and 2010 proceedings, co-author of Fundamentals of Electronic Governance (2022) and Prof. Chukut’s principal collaborator on the forum.

According to those close to the project

The idea for the Days originated with Prof. Svitlana Chukut. She drove the project day and night across all four editions. Together, Prof. Chukut and Zahvoiska personally secured the participation of sponsors, including Microsoft.

As the organisers confirmed: it was they who pioneered this system of organising symposiums and events, which became popular and was adopted by others.

Microsoft Ukraine · Lead sponsor of all four editions (2008–2011) · 2008 proceedings · 2011 archive ESET Ukraine · official partner, 2010 Softkey Ukraine · exhibition sponsor, 2010

The system

A format designed for successive editions

The editions held from 2008 to 2011 document the format developed by Prof. Svitlana Chukut and Olha Zahvoiska. According to the organisers, other events subsequently adopted aspects of this approach.

  1. 01

    A multi-format programme

    The programme combined a plenary session, thematic working groups, a technology exhibition and videoconferencing.

  2. 02

    International participation

    Ministers, ambassadors, United Nations representatives and European Commission experts took part in the discussions.

  3. 03

    Proceedings for every edition

    Published materials and proceedings documented the discussions and their outcomes.

  4. 04

    Partnership embedded in the programme

    Microsoft, ESET and Softkey supported the series. Technology companies contributed expertise, demonstrations and training activities.

  5. 05

    Educational side-programmes

    The 2010 edition included a programme for school pupils and the launch of the journal E-Governance. In 2011, Microsoft provided training for teachers.

  6. 06

    Scaling to a full week

    In 2011, the forum expanded from one day to a five-day programme encompassing conferences, round tables, exhibitions and training.

Four editions

Prof. Svitlana Chukut’s post-event reports provide the attendance figures based on paper registration. The programme and contemporary accounts identify the authorities, organisations and companies linked to each edition.

201028.04 · Kyiv

More than 400 forum participants and 300 pupils

Read the recommendations

The third edition, “Implementing E-Governance as a Prerequisite for Public Administration Reform”, brought together public institutions, software companies and international experts.

  • Six working groups, a technology exhibition and an educational programme for around 300 pupils
  • Guests included Gerardo Casini (UN) and Kerry Monaghan (USAID)
  • Official partner ESET Ukraine; exhibition sponsors Microsoft Ukraine and Softkey Ukraine
  • Launch of the first issue of the international journal E-Governance
ESET press release →

Participants included representatives of the Cabinet Secretariat, the Verkhovna Rada, executive authorities and local self-government, as well as the State Committee on Archives and the Ukrainian Research Institute of Archival Affairs and Records Management. Recommendations called for a national services portal, digital-readiness indicators, wider Internet access and use of electronic signatures, and a master’s programme and continuing education in e-governance. 2008 participants

  • The conference covered central and local e-governance, digital services and e-democracy. A technology exhibition and videoconference rounded out the programme.
  • General editor, with Olha Zahvoiska as co-editor of the 128-page proceedings

Participants recommended public services designed around residents’ needs, common data standards, privacy and security measures, accessibility and training for public servants. These recommendations were also discussed and endorsed at the TER-INFO pilot seminar at the Presidential Secretariat on 12–13 June 2008.

Recommendations and follow-up

Four editions trace the policy work from the first national framework to the practical priorities discussed at the 2011 closing round table.

2008Recommendations adopted by forum participants

Build a national framework

  • Draft a national concept and strategies for e-governance and e-democracy, backed by a dedicated government programme.
  • Redesign public services before automating them. Use common data standards, secure information exchange and mobile access.
  • Expand free internet access and accessible services. Involve residents and businesses in public decisions and train civil servants to use digital tools.

  • Align the national strategy with civil-service reform and anti-corruption work. Assign responsibilities and monitor service quality.
  • Update the rules on information, personal data, procurement and citizen appeals to support digital transactions.
  • Create a single public-services portal and produce guidance for implementation from central government to local communities.

Full 2009 summary by area

Read the document in translation

EnglishFrançais

Recommendations of the 2009 E-Governance Day

Participants at the 14 May 2009 forum addressed recommendations to the Verkhovna Rada, the Cabinet of Ministers, the Presidential Secretariat, executive authorities, the National Academy and companies working in e-governance. The proposals covered national policy, the legal framework, implementation and workforce development.

National strategy and accountability
To Parliament, the Cabinet and the Presidential Secretariat, participants proposed a national concept and strategies for e-governance and e-democracy, a dedicated state programme and coordination with public administration reform. They also proposed monitoring service quality.
Legislation and standards
To Parliament, they proposed updating laws on information and personal data, public procurement and citizen appeals to accommodate electronic requests. They also called for common IT standards and legal rules for electronic agreements and public–private partnerships.
Digital services and implementation
To the Cabinet, the State Committee for Informatization and executive authorities at all levels, they proposed a single public-services portal, free internet access points, electronic identification, digital signatures and shared standards for electronic documents. They also sought funding, public readiness indicators and support for local authorities, including district administrations.
Research and civil-service training
To the National Academy, they proposed research with its regional institutes, practical guides for different levels of government, short courses for civil servants and IT specialists, an e-governance classroom and consideration of a dedicated institute. They also proposed updating the occupational classifier to include managers of organisational e-governance systems.
Technology partners
Participants invited software developers to help implement systems in state and local government. They proposed examining financing arrangements, including deferred payment after implementation backed by state guarantees.

The forum also called for translating and applying Council of Europe Recommendation CM/Rec(2009)1 on e-democracy.

Council of Europe recommendation on e-democracy

2010Information Policy Department working proposals

Assign responsibility for implementation

  • Prepare a draft presidential decree and a Cabinet action plan with responsible institutions, deadlines and funding.
  • Set up coordination in the Cabinet Secretariat and designate implementation units in ministries and regional administrations.
  • Adapt the national informatization programme and expand civil-service training and the Academy’s master’s-level provision.

Regulatory framework

2011Discussion priorities documented in the programme and contemporary reports

Priorities from the closing round table

  • Consider a draft act on priority implementation measures and a national e-governance development strategy.
  • Improve implementation in central authorities and access to public information, including through library access points.
  • Advance digital education. The closing discussion also addressed funding, shortages of specialists and awareness of the benefits for communities.

2011 proposals on the information society and European cooperation

Two policy documents accompany the 2011 E-Governance Days. One presents proposals for the draft Presidential Address for 2011. The other sets out the Academy department’s 2011 cooperation programme with the European Union.

Proposals for the draft Presidential Address

  • Clarify responsibility for national ICT policy, align information-society indicators with EU standards, adopt common digital signature standards and establish electronic document exchange between authorities. The proposals also called for a single portal for administrative services, online business procedures and measures to implement personal data protection.
  • Expand Internet access at schools, libraries and community centres, support digital literacy and distance learning for underserved groups, and digitise archives, library collections and museum holdings.
EnglishFrançais

Cooperation programme with the European Union

  • Propose exchanges of faculty, research and curricula, placements abroad, visiting experts, a joint bachelor’s programme in Communications and Services, and professional development for civil servants and local government officials. Invite European experts to contribute to the E-Governance Days.
  • Seek European expertise for a draft national e-governance strategy, personal data protection and readiness monitoring across levels of government. The programme proposed technical assistance for rural digital education and pilots in digital cities and regions, public e-services, sectoral applications and e-democracy.

What the forum brought together

From national policy to local services

The programme connected electronic records, data protection and public-service reform with practical cases such as online permits in Slavutych and digital education in Kyiv. The closing round table collected recommendations for the Cabinet of Ministers, Parliament and the Presidential Administration.

Access to information and digital skills

Libraries showed how citizens could reach government information through local access points. Education authorities, teachers and technology companies contributed to a programme that combined classroom uses of technology, teacher training, robotics and online safety.

International exchange and industry

The opening brought together Ukrainian officials, Estonia’s ambassador and a UN representative. The programme also listed other diplomatic delegations. The technology exhibition gave public-sector and education participants an opportunity to see tools demonstrated by IT suppliers.

Authorities, institutions and companies

The Academy’s draft programme provides the roles and affiliations below. Contemporary accounts, surviving working lists and exhibition photographs add evidence where available. The lists reflect the available records and use institutional names from the period.

National authorities and agencies

  • Presidential Administration, Cabinet of Ministers Secretariat, Verkhovna Rada Committee on Freedom of Speech and Information, and the Verkhovna Rada’s Computerised Systems Directorate.
  • Ministries of Social Policy, Economic Development and Trade, and Education and Science, Youth and Sports. The working records also name the ministries of Defence, Agrarian Policy and Food, and Energy and Coal Industry.
  • Main Civil Service Department, State Agency for Science, Innovation and Informatization, State Agency for Investment and National Projects, and State Property Fund.
  • State services for special communications and information protection, personal data protection, archival affairs, financial monitoring, customs and statistics. The Academy’s account also names the National Bank and the nuclear regulator.
  • State Committee for Television and Radio Broadcasting, listed for the public information round table.

Regional and district state administrations

  • The programme listed Odesa Oblast State Administration and the education department of Novovorontsovka District State Administration.
  • Working records also identify the oblast state administrations of Donetsk, Kharkiv, Kherson, Kirovohrad, Rivne and Sumy. Education officials from several regions joined the education programme.

Local self-government

  • The programme listed the education directorate of the Kyiv City Council’s executive body (Kyiv City State Administration) and a case study on online permits in Slavutych, presented by the Entrepreneurship Support Fund.
  • The working lists identify the Odesa and Kharkiv oblast councils, the executive committees of Mykolaiv and Slavutych city councils, and the Verkhovna Rada of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea.

Collaboration in Ontario

Based in Kingston, Ontario, Canada, Prof. Svitlana Chukut is open to collaboration with colleges, universities, public-sector organisations and professional communities across Ontario, in the areas her profile demonstrates:

Target roles in Canada

  • Curriculum Developer
  • Instructional Designer
  • Digital Learning Producer
  • Academic Quality Assurance Specialist
  • Education Policy Analyst
  • Digital Government Policy Analyst
  • Curriculum and Instructional Design Consultant
  • Higher Education Accreditation and Quality Assurance Consultant
  • Digital Government and Public Sector Transformation Consultant
  • Academic Program Development Lead
  • Public Administration Professor

Instructional design & curriculum development

Competency-based programmes, online and blended courses, authentic assessment and AODA/WCAG accessibility — 17 course initiatives and 50+ modules developed at George Brown Polytechnic in Toronto.

Digital learning production

Production of digital learning content and interactive course resources for online and blended post-secondary delivery, in Brightspace (D2L) and H5P.

Digital-governance expertise & consulting

Information policy, e-governance, e-democracy and artificial intelligence in public administration — co-author of Ukraine's national Concept for the Development of E-Governance (2010).

Guest teaching & lectures

Guest courses and lectures in public administration, digital governance and communication, drawing on 25+ years of university teaching in Ukraine and Canada.

Higher education quality assurance & accreditation

Co-developed Ukraine’s national higher education standards in Public Governance and Administration for bachelor’s, master’s and PhD programs. Contributed to program licensing and accreditation and served as deputy chair of the sectoral expert council for the discipline.

Academic program leadership & graduate education

Led the Department of Theory and Practice of Management at Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute and served as academic lead for its PhD program in Public Governance and Administration (2018–2025). Coordinated faculty and program delivery and supervised graduate and doctoral research.

Research funding & peer review

Assessed competitive research proposals for the National Research Foundation of Ukraine (2021 and 2024) and Ukraine’s Ministry of Education and Science (2019–2022). Also reviewed journal manuscripts and served on dissertation defence councils.

Public service training & professional development

Designed and delivered professional training for civil servants and local-government officials on digital public services, communication with residents and e-governance implementation. Received Ukraine’s National Agency on Civil Service awards for innovation in professional training in 2020 and 2021.

To discuss a role, a project or an invitation, please use the contact channels above — email or LinkedIn.
